text:
keenan_sales: Heads-up — ACME are blocked on their Dedicated POC. GPU pool provisioning in us-central1 keeps failing, and their infra team also hit IP quota errors. They asked about pricing delta if we do a temporary burst in us-east1. Need SE + infra help.
raj_se: On it. Can you paste the API error logs from the provisioning call?
keenan_sales: Here — customer pasted from our console:```error: Allocation failed: Insufficient GPUs in zone us-central1-a. Details: requested 8xA100, available 0. Fallback attempted: none.```Also another message:```error: Could not allocate external IP: quotaExceeded."`
margo_cs: They're waiting on a quick answer for pricing (burst vs reserved) and also asked for confirmation we support KMS + audit logs for the Private deployment questionnaire. Simple yes/no will do for their Sec team.
raj_se: For pricing: reserve commit reduces monthly unit price ~25% for the committed capacity; short bursts (dedicated burst pools) bill on peak usage at on-demand rates. I can DM exact numbers but need to confirm region capacity before quoting.
tim_infra: The allocation error + IP quota indicate two independent constraints: (1) GPU availability in us-central1-a — that depends on cloud provider region pools; (2) external IP quota for the project. Quick checks: run `gcloud compute regions describe us-central1` for spare GPUs (or our internal capacity dashboard), and check project quotas for 'External IP addresses'.
raj_se: Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) Try provisioning in us-east1-b which currently has spare capacity. 2) Create ephemeral private-only endpoints (no external IP) to validate model serving while we resolve IP quota. 3) If they need external endpoints, ask customer's infra to request + increase IP quota with provider — usually fast.
keenan_sales: Customer says they can't move region due to data residency concern (must be us-central1). They also need the price delta so procurement can approve an emergency transient increase. Any way to do cross-region with VPC peering to satisfy residency?
raj_se: Residency constraints are sticky. We can propose a hybrid: control plane in us-east for quick burst and data plane pinned to us-central1 with strict routing — but that likely won't satisfy strict residency rules. If they require compute in us-central1 only, we need to resolve capacity/IP quotas there.
margo_cs: On KMS + audit logs: yes — Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS and audit exports. I can send the snippet for their questionnaire. If you want, I'll paste the standard text.
keenan_sales: Please paste it now, that'll unblock the Sec review. Also, can infra try a config tweak to reduce GPU request to 4 x A100 to see if partial pool can spin up?
tim_infra: Will try. Running:```rdwctl provision --pool dedicated --region us-central1 --zone us-central1-a --gpus 4 --type a100```I'll report back.
deploy-bot: [provision-request] request_id=rr-21a9, region=us-central1-a, gpus=4, status=allocation_failed, reason="insufficient GPUs in zone"
raj_se: If 4 also fails, next step is to attempt a zone fallback (us-central1-b/c) and coordinate with Cloud provider support to drain capacity or get a temporary allocation — that requires a provider support ticket. We can coordinate the ticket if you want.
keenan_sales: They want an ETA. If we open a provider ticket now, how long to resolution?
tim_infra: Typical provider SLA for quota/capacity requests is 4-24 hours, sometimes longer for GPUs. For IP quota increases it's usually <1 hour if validated. We'll open both tickets; please share customer contact.
raj_se: Pricing note to give procurement immediately: for a one-time 2-week burst of 8x A100 in us-central1 we estimate on-demand delta ~$13k/week vs reserved committable monthly price — tell them this is a placeholder until we confirm exact inventory/pricing.
keenan_sales: Sent customer contact in DM. Also flagged procurement that estimate is tentative.
margo_cs: Pasted Sec questionnaire snippet:```Yes — Dedicated supports CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) via KMS integrations (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK). Audit logs for model inference and admin actions can be exported to the customer's logging project or S3 bucket; retention controls available. Contact security@redwood.com for SOC/ISO package.```
keenan_sales: Perfect. Customer responded: "OK please open provider tickets — we'll wait 24 hrs. Also can you temporarily reduce GPU to 2 so we can at least load test model?"
raj_se: Lowering to 2 should be fine for basic inference validation. Recommend also switching to a smaller instance type (e.g., T4) if they only need throughput testing.
tim_infra: Running smaller attempt:```rdwctl provision --pool dedicated --region us-central1 --zone us-central1-a --gpus 2 --type a100``` -> deploy-bot: [provision-request] request_id=rr-21a9b, gpus=2, status=allocated, endpoint=10.128.23.45 (no external IP)
keenan_sales: Nice, they can run internal tests. Customer still needs external endpoints for end-to-end smoke tests — tickets opened. I'll update them.
raj_se: I'll prepare a concise pricing table for the exact SKU and send in thread once provider confirms region availability.
margo_cs: I'll follow up on the security docs if they need more (SOC2 evidence).
keenan_sales: Thanks all. Quick ask: please tag me on the provider ticket updates and post final numbers here. :thumbsup:
